text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Financial markets search stability after last Friday's plunge.
-- Credit Foncier executive Jean-Pascal Beaufret to resign after constitutional court cancels decree naming him to post because of a conflict with his former job as Treasury official.
-- Five major Club Mediterranee shareholders break core shareholder pact.

-- President Jacques Chirac and Chancellor Helmut Kohl meet today in Nuremberg, Germany on EU single currency, "stability pact" and defence issues ahead of Dublin European Union summit on Friday and Saturday.
-- Shareholding reshuffle expected at Club Mediterranee.
-- Poor consumer spending weighs on appliance manufacturer Moulinex, confirms need for restructuring plan.
-- Merger between Air France and Air Inter to be effective in September 1997, joint operations start in April.

-- Senator Jean-Pierre Fourcade says in an interview the state should compensate Social Security regime for losses which would result from payroll charge relief for employers under bill on introduction of pension funds in France.
-- WTO conference opens in Singapore today.
-- European countries divided on how to tax Chinese imports of cheap luggage and leather goods. Some say China unfairly dumping.
-- Daewoo's blocked attempt to buy Thomson Multimedia reveal some French attitudes toward business and jobs that may slow France's ability to adapt to new forms of economic competition.
